recent_articles.title: Stand-off over Bengaluru Development portfolio likely to be discussed in Delhi - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Krishna Byre Gowda**, Karnataka's Minister for Bengaluru Development, is reportedly dissatisfied with the truncated portfolio he received.  He has expressed his discontent to **Congress Central leadership**, amidst a critical monsoon season and an absence of elected councillors in Bengaluru due to delayed elections for five corporations under the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA).

recent_articles.title: GBA orders municipal corporations to prepare action plan to improve roads, junctions amid monsoon - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA)** has directed municipal corporations to prepare an action plan for improving roads and congested junctions using a ₹2,000 crore fund announced by **Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar**. The BDA will contribute 50% of the amount, while the remaining share will be provided by the State government. While residents welcome the announcement, they also point to ongoing infrastructure works causing inconvenience and highlight concerns about planning.  The GBA has directed corporations to prioritize areas with high traffic volumes and address citizen complaints regarding pedestrian infrastructure and waterlogged points.

recent_articles.title: Chief Minister travels by Metro to avoid Zero-Traffic arrangements in Bengaluru - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar** traveled by **Namma Metro** from Vidhana Soudha to Silk Institute on Sunday, June 7, 2026, to visit his home turf of Kanakapura.  He chose this method to avoid disrupting traffic for the public after recognizing the inconvenience of using zero-traffic arrangements. The decision followed a similar incident last week where **Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot**'s convoy was granted zero-traffic access at Wind Tunnel Junction, sparking public outrage and criticism about Bengaluru's infrastructure.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar keeping BDA, BMRDA to drive PRR and Bidadi Township raises questions - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar** has retained control of the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) and Bangalore Metropolitan Region Development Authority (BMRDA), despite previously assigning the portfolios to **Krishna Byre Gowda**. This decision has sparked controversy as it allows **Shivakumar** to continue overseeing key projects, including the Bengaluru Business Corridor and Bidadi Township, while **Byre Gowda** is now responsible for tunnel roads overseen by **B-SMILE**.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka: Former Ministers disappointed over not being included in Cabinet - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** leaders are facing pressure to include senior ministers from the previous Siddaramaiah Cabinet in Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar’s cabinet. **B.Z. Zameer Ahmed Khan**, a Muslim leader, was excluded from the cabinet, sparking protests and discussions among religious leaders.  The party is expected to expand its cabinet after the Rajya Sabha elections, but several senior ministers are disappointed with their lack of inclusion.

recent_articles.title: State govt. urged to prepare roadmap for comprehensively growing Kalyana Karnataka - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kalyana Karnataka Horata Samiti** urged the newly formed **D.K. Shivakumar** government to develop a time-bound roadmap and scientific action plan for comprehensive development in the Kalyana Karnataka region, covering key sectors like irrigation, industry, roads, transport, education, employment, tourism, and sports. The organization's core committee met under the chairmanship of honorary president Basavaraj Deshmukh at Kalaburagi on Sunday.

recent_articles.title: 13 out of 14 Ministers in Karnataka Cabinet are crorepatis; face criminal cases - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D.K. Shivakumar**, the Chief Minister of **Karnataka**, and 13 other Ministers in the reconstituted state cabinet have declared assets exceeding ₹206.15 crore, according to an analysis by **Association for Democratic Reforms** and **Karnataka Election Watch**. All 13 ministers have criminal cases against them, with some having serious charges.  The highest asset holder is **Shivakumar**, while **U.T. Khader Fareed** has the lowest declared assets.

recent_articles.title: The Hindu Huddle 2026 Day 2 live updates: Not competing with Indian states, I'm competing with China, Japan, etc, says Revanth Reddy - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The sixth edition of **The Hindu Group**’s annual ideas conclave, The Hindu Huddle, is being held in Bengaluru on June 5th and 6th.  **Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar** formally inaugurated the event on Friday morning. Day 1 featured discussions by leading Indian and global voices on important issues. Day 2 will include **Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy**, Members of Parliament, industry leaders, sports persons, actors, and artists.

recent_articles.title: Minister Ramalinga Reddy’s resignation issue resolved, says Chief Minister Shivakumar - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D.K. Shivakumar**, **Karnataka Chief Minister**, resolved a crisis triggered by **Ramalinga Reddy's** resignation over portfolio allocation after marathon discussions with the senior Congress leader.  The meeting, lasting nearly two-and-a-half hours, involved senior Congress leaders and some of **Reddy's** close associates.  **Shivakumar** stated that the issue was a case of miscommunication and assured that everything would be sorted out.

recent_articles.title: Ramalinga Reddy resigns from Ministry, says he is ‘humiliated’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Ramalinga Reddy**, a senior Congress legislator from Bengaluru, resigned after being denied the **Bengaluru Development** portfolio by **Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar**.  He stated that he would not personally submit his resignation but would do so through an official channel.  Reddy, who has been influential in East and North Bengaluru, expressed disappointment over the decision and claimed a promise made by **Shivakumar** to give him the portfolio was broken. Supporters of Reddy staged protests in his constituency.  Former Law and Parliamentary Affairs Minister H.K. Patil urged leaders to address the issue justly.

recent_articles.title: Kharge files nomination papers for Rajya Sabha polls from Karnataka - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mallikarjun Kharge**, president of the **All India Congress Committee**, filed his nomination papers for the Rajya Sabha election from Karnataka, accompanied by **Rahul Gandhi**. The other two candidates are **Mansoor Ali Khan** and **Pawan Khera**.  The elections will be held on June 18th with the Congress party expected to secure three seats. Discussions regarding portfolio allocation among ministers were reportedly underway during a car ride.

recent_articles.title: CM asks officials to protect voters’ rights during SIR - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar** held a meeting with senior officials to discuss the upcoming Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Karnataka. He emphasized protecting voting rights during the process, urging officials to establish SIR help desks and provide necessary documentation assistance to voters who may need it. **Shivakumar** expressed concern about voter disenfranchisement in previous SIRs across other states, emphasizing his commitment to ensuring this does not occur in Karnataka.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka cabinet portfolios allocated, but disgruntlement remains - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mr. Shivakumar**, the newly sworn-in **Karnataka** Chief Minister, allocated portfolios to his cabinet on Thursday (June 5, 2026).  The most contested portfolio, Bengaluru Development, was given to **Krishna Byre Gowda**. Senior Minister **Ramalinga Reddy** received Major and Medium Irrigation. **Priyank Kharge** will be the new Home Minister, while **G. Parameshwara** has been assigned Revenue and Sports. **Eshwar Khandre** is in charge of Rural Development and Panchayat Raj, and **Byrathi Suresh** holds Transport.  The allocation of Bengaluru Development portfolio remains a contentious issue.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka cabinet portfolios allocated, but disgruntlement remains - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mr. Shivakumar**, the newly-sworn in **Karnataka** Chief Minister, allocated portfolios to his cabinet on Thursday after a day of negotiations and discontent among some ministers.  **Krishna Byre Gowda** received the coveted Bengaluru Development portfolio previously held by Mr. Shivakumar. **Ramalinga Reddy**, who had sought the portfolio, was given Major and Medium Irrigation. Other key changes included **Priyank Kharge** as Home Minister and **G. Parameshwara** as Revenue and Sports Minister. The allocation of the Bengaluru Development portfolio is likely to remain a contentious issue in the lead-up to upcoming civic polls.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar announces exclusive secretariats to address public grievances, issues of NRIs - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D.K. Shivakumar**, the new Chief Minister of **Karnataka**, met with senior officials on Thursday to discuss his government's priorities. He announced plans for two exclusive secretariats: one to address public grievances and another to handle issues related to NRIs.  He also directed district in-charge Secretaries to submit proposals within 25 days, and asked all departments to create action plans within 15 days on programs listed in the State Budget. **Shivakumar** emphasized transparency and adherence to legal frameworks while addressing concerns about misuse of government schemes like the Gruha Jyothi program. He also instructed police to establish anti-rowdy squads in every taluk.

recent_articles.title: Will usher in ‘Yuva Yuga’, promises new Karnataka Chief Minister - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar** announced a series of new programs aimed at addressing unemployment, rural distress, and youth development in Karnataka. These include the establishment of a private employment exchange, funding for 10,000 Bharat Jodo Yuvakara Sanghas, and a waiver for completion certificates to ensure electricity and water connections for properties violating building bylaws. The new programs are expected to cost at least ₹3,250 crore.

recent_articles.title: BK Hariprasad Replaces DK Shivakumar As Karnataka Congress Chief
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **B.K. Hariprasad**, a veteran Congress leader, has been appointed as the new President of the **Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC)** by **AICC President Mallikarjun Kharge**.  He replaces **D.K. Shivakumar**, who resigned from the position after six years in charge and contributed to the party's victory in 2023.  Hariprasad, known for his criticism of Hindutva organizations and the BJP, is a former Member of the Rajya Sabha and has served as a Member of the Karnataka Legislative Council.

recent_articles.title: D.K. Shivakumar sworn-in as 25th Chief Minister of Karnataka - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D.K. Shivakumar**, the newly elected **Chief Minister of Karnataka**, was sworn in on Wednesday, June 3, 2026, alongside **G. Parameshwara** as Deputy Chief Minister.  The swearing-in ceremony took place at Glass House in Lok Bhavan and saw the inclusion of 13 Cabinet ministers, with a focus on senior party members. The event was attended by prominent figures from across the political spectrum, including Rahul Gandhi and Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu. Shivakumar's administration will face challenges as it navigates the upcoming Rajya Sabha and Karnataka Legislative Council elections.

recent_articles.title: How the D-day unfolded for DKS, reaching across political divide - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D.K. Shivakumar**, the newly sworn-in Chief Minister of Karnataka, began his day with personal and political gestures, including calls to MLAs and a visit to former Chief Ministers **B.S. Yediyurappa** and **H.D. Deve Gowda**. He chose traditional attire for his oath ceremony and invited Congress leaders **Rahul Gandhi**, **Mallikarjun Kharge**, and **Sonia Gandhi** to the event, which was attended by high-ranking members of the **Congress** party from other states.  The ceremony also included a gathering of religious leaders representing various faiths.

recent_articles.title: Make Satish Jarkiholi KPCC president, say AHINDA district units - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **AHINDA** leaders and various organizations in Karnataka have demanded that **Minister Satish Jarkiholi** be appointed as the **Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) president**. They argue that this would strengthen the AHINDA movement and ensure support from all deprived communities.  The demands come after **Jarkiholi**'s successful track record in organizing the AHINDA movement and his popularity among various communities, including Muslims.

recent_articles.title: Meeting between Zameer Ahmed Khan and D.K. Suresh raises eyebrows in Karnataka - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **B.Z. Zameer Ahmed Khan** met with former **MP D.K. Suresh** in a closed-door meeting that sparked speculation about political fallout from an audio clip purportedly featuring him discussing sabotage of the Davangere South bypoll election chances.  Congress leaders from Davangere have called for action against **Khan**, citing the audio as evidence of anti-party activities, while **Shamanur**, the winning Congress candidate, has urged party leadership to verify the clip's authenticity.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka CM swearing-in LIVE: D.K. Shivakumar to be sworn in as Karnataka CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D.K. Shivakumar**, the eight-time legislator and **Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee president**, will be sworn in as the 34th Chief Minister of Karnataka on Wednesday evening at Lok Bhavan.  The list of Cabinet ministers, expected to number between 10 and 15, will be released by the **Congress central leadership** on Wednesday. The event will also include prominent figures like **Rahul Gandhi**, **Mallikarjun Kharge**, and other **Congress Chief Ministers**.

recent_articles.title: D.K. Shivakumar: How the ‘rock’ of Congress became Karnataka CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **DKShi**, the eight-time MLA and prominent Congress leader in Karnataka, is poised to become the state's new chief minister following **Siddaramaiah's** resignation.  Known for his strong Hindu cultural beliefs and frequent use of the phrase "Efforts may fail, but prayers do not," **DKShi** has been a key strategist for the party in South India.

recent_articles.title: ​Change in arrangement: On the leadership transition in Karnataka - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D.K. Shivakumar**, the prominent face of the **Congress** in Karnataka, is set to become Chief Minister on June 3rd after a long-held ambition. The party's decision appears to address grievances among his supporters and aims for a successful transition ahead of the 2028 Assembly elections.  The change in leadership comes amidst anti-incumbency sentiment and with an eye towards potential alliances with the **BJP** and **JD(S)**, both of which are likely to benefit from this move. Shivakumar's success will depend on his ability to unite the party and address regional disparities while maintaining fiscal discipline.

recent_articles.title: Stage set for D.K. Shivakumar to over as new CM of Karnataka - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D.K. Shivakumar**, the eight-time legislator and Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee president, will be sworn in as the 34th Chief Minister of Karnataka on Wednesday evening at Lok Bhavan.  The list of Cabinet ministers is expected to be released by the **Congress central leadership** on Wednesday, with speculation about new faces joining the existing cabinet. The event will be attended by prominent leaders like **Rahul Gandhi**, **Mallikarjun Kharge**, and other state chief ministers. Traffic restrictions are in place for the ceremony in Bengaluru.

recent_articles.title: List of Ministers to be sworn in with DKS to be finalised only June 3 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** central leadership is expected to announce the list of Cabinet ministers, including D.K. Shivakumar, on Wednesday morning.  The final list may include between 10 and 15 ministers, with negotiations ongoing regarding the Deputy Chief Minister's post and the creation of a coordination committee. **Siddaramaiah** and **Shivakumar** have been meeting with the central leadership to finalize their preferences for cabinet positions and the Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee president.  The expansion of the Cabinet is expected to occur after the Rajya Sabha polls, pending consensus on regional and caste combinations.

recent_articles.title: Will CM-designate Shivakumar continue to hold charge of Bengaluru Development portfolio? - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Will D.K. Shivakumar**, the Chief Minister, faces pushback from **Congress Ministers** in Bengaluru who advocate for a full-time minister for the city's development portfolio.  Senior ministers like **Ramalinga Reddy**, **K.J. George**, and **Krishna Byre Gowda** are mentioned as potential candidates. While Shivakumar is keen to retain the portfolio, some argue his personal involvement has been significant in driving key projects and shaping Bengaluru's governance.

recent_articles.title: DKS as CM may provide big push to tunnel roads, PRR and Bidadi township - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D.K. Shivakumar**, the soon-to-be Chief Minister of Karnataka, has sparked both optimism and concern regarding his plans for infrastructure development in the city.  He is advocating for large-scale projects like the Twin Tunnel Roads, Peripheral Ring Road, and Bidadi Township, which have faced financial hurdles and land acquisition challenges. While some see these initiatives as crucial for Bengaluru's future growth, others fear they will displace farmers and disregard public opposition. **V. Ravichandar**, a member of Brand Bengaluru Committee, believes Shivakumar envisions himself as the successor to former Chief Minister S.M. Krishna, focusing on peripherally-located projects to accommodate urban expansion.  Activist Vinay Sreenivasa expresses concern about Shivakumar's potential disregard for opposition and his preference for a capital-intensive development model that may negatively impact the poor.

recent_articles.title: Political leaders hail victorious RCB, Siddaramaiah appeals for adhering to safety guidelines - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **RCB**, the Royal Challengers Bengaluru, won their second IPL Championship trophy, prompting congratulatory messages from **Siddaramaiah**, the caretaker Chief Minister of Karnataka, and **D.K. Shivakumar**, the Chief Minister-designate.  **H. D. Kumaraswamy**, a Union Minister, praised the team's consistency and character, highlighting the contributions of players like **Virat Kohli** and **Bhuvaneshwar Kumar**.

recent_articles.title: Ministry formation to be done in phases while discussions will shift to Delhi - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mallikarjun Kharge**, **All India Congress Committee president**, stated that the formation of the Karnataka Cabinet will be done in phases, with no official proposal specifying the number of ministers yet received.  He indicated that decisions regarding cabinet size and Deputy Chief Ministers will be made after a concrete proposal is submitted to the central leadership.  **D.K. Shivakumar**, newly elected leader of the Congress Legislature Party, and **outgoing Chief Minister Siddaramaiah** are expected to present their choices for Cabinet positions to the central leadership on Monday.

recent_articles.title: Siddaramaiah has set an example in contemporary politics by handing over power gracefully, says KPCC spokesperson - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **H.A. Venkatesh**, spokesperson for the **Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC)**, praised outgoing Chief Minister Siddaramaiah for his smooth and graceful transition of power.  Venkatesh lauded Siddaramaiah's commitment to principled politics and his welfare-oriented administration, highlighting the success of the five guarantee schemes implemented during his tenure. He also acknowledged the contributions of senior Congress leaders **D.K. Shivakumar** and **G. Parameshwara**, who played key roles in designing and implementing these schemes, leading to the party's victory in 2023.  Venkatesh expressed confidence that under the leadership of Shivakumar and Parameshwara, the Congress government will continue to serve the people effectively.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka: Search for new KPCC chief has begun, says All India Congress Committee president Mallikarjun Kharge - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mallikarjun Kharge**, **All India Congress Committee president**, stated that discussions are underway to find a successor for the outgoing **Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) chief D.K. Shivakumar**.  The party is considering various candidates, including **Satish Jarkiholi**, and will prioritize a dynamic leader with strong organizational skills. The appointment of Deputy Chief Ministers and the Bengaluru Development portfolio are also being discussed, creating complications due to the emergence of **K.H. Muniyappa** as a contender for the position.  The party is considering forming a coordination committee headed by outgoing Chief Minister **Siddaramaiah** to address contentious issues.

recent_articles.title: Vatal takes exception to Governor’s letter written in English to DKS for oath ceremony - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Vatal Nagaraj**, a Kannada activist, criticized the **Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot** for inviting **D.K. Shivakumar** for the oath ceremony in English, stating it reflects a lack of respect for Kannada.  He also expressed disapproval of the Congress high command's treatment of former Chief Minister **Siddaramaiah**, accusing them of disrespecting him and forcing his resignation.

recent_articles.title: DK Shivakumar to become new Karnataka CM after being elected state CLP leader; oath ceremony on 3 June | Today News
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **DK Shivakumar**, the **Congress party's** Karnataka president, was elected as the leader of the Congress Legislature Party (CLP) on Saturday.  The CLP meeting at Vidhana Soudha saw outgoing Chief Minister Siddaramaiah propose Shivakumar's name for the post, which was unanimously accepted by the party members. The swearing-in ceremony is scheduled for June 3rd and will be held at the Glass House in Lok Bhavan, Bengaluru. Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot invited **Shivakumar** to take oath as Karnataka CM along with his team on June 3rd.

recent_articles.title: Congress will face setback in 2028 Assembly elections: Former BJP MLA Narasimha Naik - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Narasimha Naik**, a former **BJP** MLA, stated that the **Congress** will face a setback in the 2028 Assembly elections without outgoing Chief Minister Siddaramaiah.  He expressed disappointment over Mr. Siddaramaiah's resignation and believes it will be a challenge for the new leader, **D.K. Shivakumar**, to lead the party effectively. Naik compared this situation to former Chief Minister B.S. Yediyurappa's resignation, suggesting that the **Congress** will face similar consequences.

recent_articles.title: Congress will face setback in 2028 Assembly elections: Former BJP MLA Narasimha Naik - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Narasimha Naik**, former **BJP** MLA, claims that the **Congress** will face a setback in the 2028 Assembly elections without outgoing Chief Minister **Siddaramaiah**.  He argues that **Siddaramaiah's** forced resignation weakens the party and presents challenges for new leader **D.K. Shivakumar**. Naik believes this situation mirrors the impact of former Chief Minister **B.S. Yediyurappa's** resignation, suggesting a potential victory for the **BJP** in 2028.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka: Amid hectic discussions, curiosity grows over new Cabinet formation - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D.K. Shivakumar**, the newly elected Chief Minister of Karnataka, is expected to form a Cabinet with 8 to 10 members sworn in on June 3rd. The composition will prioritize representation from major castes and communities within the ruling **Congress**. A full Cabinet is anticipated after elections for four Rajya Sabha seats and seven Legislative Council seats on June 18th.

recent_articles.title: D.K. Shivakumar meets Governor Gehlot, stakes claim to form new govt in Karnataka - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D.K. Shivakumar**, the newly elected leader of the **Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee**, will be sworn in as Chief Minister on Wednesday, June 3rd at Lok Bhavan. The event is expected to be attended by the central leadership of the party and Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot has invited him to take the oath at 4:05 p.m.  The power transition was overseen by **Mallikarjun Kharge**, **Rahul Gandhi**, and **Sonia Gandhi**.  With Cabinet formation still under discussion, speculation remains about whether a full Cabinet will be sworn in and if there will be deputy Chief Ministers.

recent_articles.title: D.K. Shivakumar to be sworn-in as Karnataka chief minister at Glass House in Lok Bhavan on June 3 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D.K. Shivakumar**, the newly elected chief minister of Karnataka, will have his swearing-in ceremony at **Glass House** in **Bengaluru** on June 3rd.  **G.C. Chandrashekar**, **KPCC Working President**, stated that the decision to hold a simple oath-taking ceremony was made by the **Congress Legislative Party (CLP)** and that party workers are not required to attend. The event follows intense negotiations in New Delhi regarding power distribution among factions, with the CLP meeting scheduled for May 30th.

recent_articles.title: Shivakumar’s elevation as Karnataka CM poses existential challenge for JD(S) - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **H.D. Kumaraswamy** and **D.K. Shivakumar**, both members of the Vokkaliga community, are facing a potential political challenge as the change in leadership within Karnataka's Congress-led government raises concerns for the **Janata Dal (Secular)**. The party is considering possible decisions that could see **Kumaraswamy** return to full-time State politics, which some view as disadvantageous given his rivalry with **Shivakumar**.

recent_articles.title: Siddaramaiah and D.K. Shivakumar: A public bonhomie that never let up - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Despite internal tensions within the **Congress** in Karnataka, **Siddaramaiah** and **Shivakumar**, leaders of opposing factions, maintained a cordial public image.  They were seen discussing power transfer in Delhi and even embraced after **Siddaramaiah's** resignation. Their unity was evident throughout their tenure, with frequent appearances together and gestures of support for each other. The transition of power from **Siddaramaiah** to **Shivakumar**, though initially feared to be messy, unfolded smoothly.

recent_articles.title: Will Siddaramaiah's breakfast with Cabinet colleagues on May 28 end with leadership change in Karnataka? - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Siddaramaiah**, the Chief Minister of Karnataka, has invited his Cabinet colleagues for a breakfast meeting on Thursday to address speculation about his future.  The Congress high command has asked him to move to the Rajya Sabha, paving the way for a leadership change. **Randeep Singh Surjewala**, the All India Congress Committee general secretary in charge of Karnataka, arrived in Bengaluru to facilitate the transition process. While some party members are pushing for his resignation, he has refused to comment on the matter and only stated that he will speak tomorrow.

recent_articles.title: Leadership tussle in Karnataka: Congress high command wants Siddaramaiah to move to Rajya Sabha, sources say, even as party officially denies - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Siddaramaiah**, the current Chief Minister of **Karnataka**, is facing pressure to step down after a meeting with the **Congress** high command in New Delhi. The discussions centered on selecting candidates for Rajya Sabha and Legislative Council elections, but sources suggest that leadership change was also a key topic.  Despite official denials, there are indications that the party may be considering a shift in leadership if **Siddaramaiah** doesn't agree to step down.  The high command is facing pressure to make a decision before June 8th deadline for Rajya Sabha nominations.

recent_articles.title: Disambiguating a year of flux: expert panels at The Hindu Huddle, 2026 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The sixth edition of The Hindu Group's ideas conclave, The Hindu Huddle, will be held in Bengaluru on June 5 and 6, 2026.  **Siddaramaiah**, **D.K. Shivakumar**, and other Chief Ministers from across the country will participate alongside Union Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship **Jayant Chaudhary**, **Omar Abdullah**, **A. Revanth Reddy**, and **K.G. Arunraj**. The event will feature discussions on topics such as tariffs' impact on the Indian economy, diplomacy in managing crises, and artificial intelligence's influence on various aspects of life.  **The Hindu Huddle** is presented by the Sami-Sabinsa Group and co-powered by the Government of Telangana.

recent_articles.title: Vijay should strongly oppose Mekedatu dam plan: Seeman - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Seeman**, chief co-ordinator of **Naam Tamilar Katchi**, criticized **D.K. Shivakumar**, Karnataka's deputy Chief Minister, for his statement that Tamil Nadu does not have the right to oppose the Karnataka government's plan to build a dam at Mekedatu across the Cauvery river.  **Seeman** called the statement arrogant and said it indicated an attempt by **Karnataka** to claim exclusive ownership over the Cauvery river water rights. He urged **Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay** to register strong opposition to the project.

recent_articles.title: Congress asks its rank and file to be alert against deletion of voters ahead of SIR exercise in Karnataka - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** leaders are concerned about the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise in Karnataka, fearing voter suppression similar to what happened in West Bengal. The party has urged its rank and file to remain vigilant and is preparing for potential challenges. **Randeep Surjewala**, Congress general secretary in charge of Karnataka, emphasized the importance of educating voters about SIR's implications.  The State government is expected to respond to the concerns raised by the party soon.

recent_articles.title: Will TVK government take ‘firm stand’ on Mekedatu project, asks Palaniswami - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Edappadi K. Palaniswami**, general secretary of the **AIADMK**, questioned the **Tamil Nadu** government's ability to protect its interests in the **Mekedatu balancing reservoir project** on the Cauvery river, citing the reported support of the **Congress** party and concerns about potential power-sharing agreements.  **D.K. Shivakumar**, Karnataka’s Deputy Chief Minister, reportedly stated that Tamil Nadu had no right to object to the project, while **T.T.V. Dhinakaran**, founder of the **AMMK**, echoed these concerns.

recent_articles.title: D.K. Shivakumar challenges BJP leaders to travel by public transport daily - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D.K. Shivakumar**, Deputy Chief Minister of **Karnataka**, criticized **BJP** leaders for using public transport only for photoshoots in response to the Prime Minister's call for austerity measures. He challenged them to travel by public transport daily, questioning the sincerity of their actions.  He also addressed the Prime Minister's call to abstain from buying gold and expressed his commitment to visit Delhi when called upon by **Rahul Gandhi**, Leader of the Opposition.

recent_articles.title: Bypolls in Davangere South and Bagalkot could witness intense battle - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article:
The **Karnataka** government has announced byelections to the Davangere South and Bagalkot Assembly constituencies on April 9.  These seats, currently held by the ruling **Congress**, are expected to be fiercely contested by the opposition **BJP**. The counting of votes will take place on May 4th. The byelections were necessitated due to the deaths of former Ministers **Shamanur Shivashankarappa** and **H.Y. Meti**.  The announcement comes amidst the Budget session, which ends on March 27th. Both the ruling party and the opposition have a week to finalize their candidates before the nomination deadline on March 23rd.

The byelection is significant for both parties as it offers an opportunity to gain ground in the state's political landscape. The **Congress** is facing internal challenges with leadership uncertainty between Chief Minister **Siddaramaiah** and Deputy Chief Minister **D.K. Shivakumar**.  The ruling party is also grappling with issues of internal reservation among Scheduled Castes and reduction of reservation for Scheduled Tribes. Meanwhile, the **BJP** aims to leverage public dissatisfaction over alleged lack of development and government policies, positioning the byelections as a vote against the current dispensation. 

Both constituencies have seen shifting fortunes in recent years.  In Bagalkot, the BJP has won four out of six elections since 1999. The late **H.Y. Meti**, a former minister and five-time legislator, had previously won from Guledgudda. In Davangere South, a newly formed constituency after delimitation in 2008, the late **Shamanur Shivaranakappa** won all four elections since then. The **Congress** is facing internal challenges in selecting a candidate for Davangere South, with family members of the deceased leader vying for the ticket.  The party's leadership will need to navigate these tensions while also considering the wishes of Muslim leaders who are pushing for a Muslim candidate in the constituency.

He emphasized that the elections are scheduled for May and urged attendees at a preparatory meeting on Sunday (March 15) to focus on voter list discrepancies, community engagement, and understanding their wards before focusing on individual tickets.  The meeting was attended by over 950 aspirants and several city Congress leaders. **Shivakumar** stressed the importance of visiting every house in their respective wards, getting to know voters, and building a strong connection with them. He stated that he would personally monitor dedicated workers and select candidates from among them.

Following his memorandum to the State Election Commissioner **G.S. Sangreshi** in February regarding voter list revision concerns, the process of correcting the voter roll has been initiated.  More than 1,500 aspirants have expressed interest in contesting the civic body polls by submitting applications. The final ward reservation notification was published by the state government on March 15, 2026. Ticket announcements are expected to follow the official election date announcement.

recent_articles.rephrased_article:
## Karnataka to Meet with MPs Over Upper Krishna Project Dispute

Karnataka's Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and other ministers will travel to Delhi this week to discuss objections raised by Andhra Pradesh regarding the Upper Krishna Project (UKP).  The trip follows a letter from Andhra Pradesh objecting to land acquisition for the project, prompting a response from the Union government seeking clarification from Karnataka. Despite these concerns, Shivakumar emphasized that the state is proceeding with the UKP as per a Tribunal order and has already invested ₹26,000 crore in its development.  He also highlighted that the state is preparing to utilize its allotted water quota according to the 2010 Tribunal award. Additionally, Karnataka is facing friction with Andhra Pradesh over the construction of a balancing reservoir on Tungabadhra, which is contributing to a loss of 30 tmcft of water for the state.
